boundary_rationale: The single verse “Sing, you heavens, for Yahweh has done it! Shout, you lower parts of the earth! Break out into singing, you mountains, O forest, all of your trees, for Yahweh has redeemed Jacob, and will glorify himself in Israel.” (web:Isa.44.23) is an imperative hymn call to the cosmos, spliced at רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier), set apart from the exhortation before it by its shift from second-person address (‘you are my servant’) to an imperative summons of heavens, earth, and mountains -- a doxology-closure unit for the redemption announcement that precedes it, standing just ahead of the fresh koh-amar self-predication that opens web:Isa.44.24. The petuchah after this verse (oshb:Isa.44.23, single-witness, tier-3) closes the layer's section on the FAR side of the row's own closing seam, grouping Isa.44.21-Isa.44.23 with the koh-amar oracle that follows rather than corroborating the isolation argued here; the cut itself rests on the addressee turn, not on that tier-3 layer.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading merges this doxology into the exhortation of Isa.44.21-Isa.44.22 as its closing acclamation rather than isolating it as its own hymn row.
literature_type_guess: one-verse doxology closing the redemption announcement

device_notes: The verse is held as its own isolable doxology-closure unit on the strength of its imperative cosmic-summons form, distinct from both the second-person exhortation before it and the koh-amar self-predication after it. A redeemer catchword straddles both of the row's own seams at root/skeleton level, not as a byte-identical refrain: כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ (oshb:Isa.44.22, byte tier) before it, the row's own כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier), and גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Isa.44.24, byte tier) after it -- a device that argues continuity across both seams without disturbing the cut, which rests on the addressee turn.

boundary_rationale: A second, distinct koh-amar frame opens the row at “Yahweh says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held” (web:Isa.45.1), spliced at כֹּה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לִמְשִׁיחוֹ֮ לְכ֣וֹרֶשׁ (oshb:Isa.45.1, byte tier) -- Cyrus's other named site in the book, a fresh verse-initial messenger formula naming its own addressee, distinct from the participle standing inside the preceding row's own frame-chain. Direct second-person address itself opens one verse later, אֲנִי֙ לְפָנֶ֣יךָ אֵלֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.45.2, byte tier). The commission runs through the purpose clause “that you may know that it is I, Yahweh, who calls you by your name” (web:Isa.45.3) and the naming עַבְדִּ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּחִירִ֑י (oshb:Isa.45.4, byte tier), “For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel my chosen” (web:Isa.45.4) -- Jacob named servant, Israel named chosen -- to the exclusive-deity formula “I am Yahweh, and there is no one else.” (web:Isa.45.6). One of the row's verses, web:Isa.45.2, is a ketiv/qere site (K/Q). The row closes on the heavens-and-earth imperative “Rain, you heavens, from above...I, Yahweh, have created it.” (web:Isa.45.8), just ahead of the paired hoy onset that opens web:Isa.45.9.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading isolates the closing rain-and-righteousness call of Isa.45.8 as its own short doxology-closure unit, on the model of Isa.44.23's imperative summons to heavens and earth, rather than holding it inside the Cyrus commission.
literature_type_guess: royal commission oracle to Cyrus closing on a creation-imperative call
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Isa.45.8 lacks a koh-amar or fresh addressee marker of its own, so the row keeps it inside the Cyrus oracle as its closing cadence rather than granting it a separate hymn row; the alternate split is disclosed above.

boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar frame answers the woe pair at “Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel and his Maker says:” (web:Isa.45.11), spliced at כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְיֹצְר֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.45.11, byte tier), turning the potter-clay challenge into the article-marked object הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת שְׁאָל֔וּנִי (oshb:Isa.45.11, byte tier) followed by the summons תְּצַוֻּֽנִי (oshb:Isa.45.11, byte tier) -- a prefix-conjugation form carrying the same first-person object suffix as the summons before it -- with no interrogative particle or pronoun standing anywhere in the verse, unlike the genuine interrogative he opening the woe pair itself, הֲיֹאמַ֨ר (oshb:Isa.45.9, byte tier). “You ask me about the things that are to come, concerning my sons, and you command me concerning the work of my hands!” (web:Isa.45.11) The unit closes on the unnamed ‘he’ who “He shall build my city, and he shall let my exiles go free” (web:Isa.45.13), a Cyrus-recalling promise without naming him again, just ahead of the next koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.45.14.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading classes this unit as a salvation oracle rather than a trial speech, on the strength of its closing city-building and exile-release promise, since the disputation frame is brief and gives way quickly to restoration language.
literature_type_guess: disputation answering the potter-clay challenge, closing on renewed commission language

device_notes: The row is argued as trial_speech on its summons-and-command shape (the article-marked object followed by the paired first-person-suffixed verbs, ‘you command me concerning the work of my hands’) rather than a question form; no morphology layer is staged to fix whether the summons form carries imperative or indicative force, so that reading is held open. The salvation-oracle rival is disclosed above and the choice between the two is held loosely.

boundary_rationale: A messenger-formula onset opens the row -- the fourth of five koh-amar frames in this run of oracles, opening at Isa.44.24, Isa.45.1, Isa.45.11, Isa.45.14 and Isa.45.18 (sweep: 5 verses) -- “Yahweh says: "The labor of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia...will come over to you” (web:Isa.45.14), spliced at כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה יְגִ֨יעַ מִצְרַ֥יִם (oshb:Isa.45.14, byte tier; the verse also carries the row's paseq mark, single-witness -- the inventory records a count there without recording position). The nations' confession “Surely God is in you; and there is no one else.” (web:Isa.45.14) runs to Israel's own vindication “Israel will be saved by Yahweh with an everlasting salvation. You will not be disappointed nor confounded to ages everlasting.” (web:Isa.45.17), just ahead of the fifth koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.45.18.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading treats the idol-makers' shame at Isa.45.16 as opening a distinct short judgment unit against the nations rather than reading it as this oracle's own turn on the way to Israel's vindication.
literature_type_guess: salvation oracle announcing the nations' submission and Israel's everlasting salvation

device_notes: The nations' own confession (‘Surely God is in you’) is kept inside this oracle as reported speech rather than treated as a second, independent trial-speech voice. The addressee itself turns at the seam -- feminine singular through Isa.45.14, עָלַ֤יִךְ יַעֲבֹ֨רוּ֙ וְלָ֣ךְ יִֽהְי֔וּ (oshb:Isa.45.14, byte tier) and אַ֣ךְ בָּ֥ךְ אֵ֛ל (oshb:Isa.45.14, byte tier), to masculine singular opening Isa.45.15, אָכֵ֕ן אַתָּ֖ה אֵ֣ל מִסְתַּתֵּ֑ר (oshb:Isa.45.15, byte tier) -- and MT 45:15 is held inside the unit as the continuation of the reported confession itself, that reported-speech frame doing the work; the honest absence to cite there is that no fresh messenger frame opens at Isa.45.15.

boundary_rationale: A messenger-formula onset opens the row -- the fifth of five koh-amar frames in this run of oracles, opening at Isa.44.24, Isa.45.1, Isa.45.11, Isa.45.14 and Isa.45.18 (sweep: 5 verses) -- “For Yahweh who created the heavens...says: "I am Yahweh. There is no other.” (web:Isa.45.18), spliced at כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר יְ֠הוָה בּוֹרֵ֨א הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם (oshb:Isa.45.18, byte tier). The self-declaration continues in the same first-person voice, “I have not spoken in secret...I, Yahweh, speak righteousness. I declare things that are right.” (web:Isa.45.19), standing just ahead of the imperative summons to the nations' survivors that opens web:Isa.45.20.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading carries this self-declaration straight into the summons that follows at Isa.45.20 as one trial speech without a fresh frame break, since both share the same exclusive-deity vocabulary and no koh-amar frame reopens there.

device_notes: The row is cut ahead of Isa.45.20 on the strength of that verse's own fresh onset, הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Isa.45.20, byte tier) -- three plural imperative forms followed by the named addressed group, a tier-1 signal standing alone -- even though the seam is not marked by a fresh koh-amar frame of its own. This row's own span carries no vocative and no second-person form at all: its offspring-of-Jacob phrase stands as the indirect object of a negated report, לֹ֥א אָמַ֛רְתִּי לְזֶ֥רַע יַעֲקֹ֖ב תֹּ֣הוּ בַקְּשׁ֑וּנִי (oshb:Isa.45.19, byte tier), inside the quoted speech being denied, not an address to that offspring. The joined-speech alternative is disclosed above.

boundary_rationale: The address turns to imperative summons at “Assemble yourselves and come. Draw near together, you who have escaped from the nations.” (web:Isa.45.20), spliced at הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Isa.45.20, byte tier) -- a fresh addressee (the nations' survivors) taking up the declare-and-witness imperative pair הַגִּ֣ידוּ וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ (oshb:Isa.45.21, byte tier), “Declare and present it...Who has shown this from ancient time?” (web:Isa.45.21), whose skeleton matches the same imperative pair opening the earlier trial speeches at Isa.41.22 and Isa.41.23 (sweep: 6 verses book-wide carry that shared skeleton). The universal appeal “Look to me, and be saved, all the ends of the earth” (web:Isa.45.22) runs to the closing verdict “All the offspring of Israel will be justified in Yahweh, and will rejoice!” (web:Isa.45.25), the row's own closing verse; the next verse opens a different subject with the ordinary burden noun מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier), not one of the verse-initial oracle headers.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading keeps this summons joined to the self-declaration of Isa.45.18-Isa.45.19 as one extended trial speech rather than cutting a fresh unit at the imperative address to the nations' survivors.

boundary_rationale: This part opens on Babylon's own gods collapsing: “Bel bows down. Nebo stoops. Their idols are carried by animals, and on the livestock. The things that you carried around are heavy loads, a burden for the weary.” (web:Isa.46.1) sets the idols of Bel and Nebo onto pack animals as dead weight, their load named with the ordinary carrying-noun מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) -- a burden common noun in this idol-procession scene, not a verse-initial oracle header of the massa series. The same noun recurs as the idols themselves cannot rescue what they carry: “They stoop and they bow down together. They could not deliver the burden, but they have gone into captivity.” (web:Isa.46.2), spliced at מַלֵּ֣ט מַשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte tier) -- the burden noun here matching Isa.46.1's at accent-stripped tier only, not byte (tipcha there against etnachta here) -- closing the tableau on their own captivity. Two root-level devices bridge into the following verses that an English gloss alone would leave undisclosed: the load-bearer participles נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1) answered by הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ מִנִּי בֶ֔טֶן הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים מִנִּי רָֽחַם (oshb:Isa.46.3) -- disjoint under consonantal search, the plene and defective spellings each standing in exactly 1 verse at skeleton tier, so the tie is root-level and not a form recurrence -- and the rescue root at Isa.46.2 answered by וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4), skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide). Neither device is treated as reason enough to hold this tableau and the following address in one unit, since web:Isa.46.3 turns the discourse from third-person description to a first-person vocative with a named addressee, the stronger seam signal here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading merges this tableau with the divine carry-claim that follows at Isa.46.3-Isa.46.4, since the same carry/bear root spans both, but the fresh vocative address at Isa.46.3 is read as the stronger boundary signal.
literature_type_guess: third-person taunt-tableau of Babylon's collapsing idol-procession
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The massa-family noun at web:Isa.46.1 and web:Isa.46.2 is read here as the ordinary burden noun of the idol-procession scene, kept apart from the verse-initial oracle-header use of the same root at the book's massa series openings. The setumah after Isa.46.2 (single-witness, tier-3) falls on this row's own back seam, terminating the row's closing verse, rather than standing as an interior division.

boundary_rationale: A fresh vocative opens this row: “Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that have been carried from their birth, that have been carried from the womb.” (web:Isa.46.3), שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier), turning from the idols' own collapse (web:Isa.46.1-Isa.46.2) to Yahweh's own first-person carry-claim, “Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.” (web:Isa.46.4) -- וַאֲנִ֣י אֶשָּׂ֔א (oshb:Isa.46.4, byte tier) answers the very carry/bear root that named the idols' load, a deliberate contrast rather than a seam; the rescue root at Isa.46.2 is likewise answered here, וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4), skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide), undisclosed at this row's own front seam until now. The comparison challenge “To whom will you compare me, and consider my equal, and compare me, as if we were the same?” (web:Isa.46.5) and the self-declaration “Remember the former things of old; for I am God, and there is no other. I am God, and there is none like me.” (web:Isa.46.9), אָנֹכִ֥י אֵל֙ וְאֵ֣ין ע֔וֹד (oshb:Isa.46.9, byte tier), carry the disputation forward through the appeal opening web:Isa.46.8 and the Cyrus prediction “I call a ravenous bird from the east, the man of my counsel from a far country. Yes, I have spoken. I will also bring it to pass. I have planned. I will also do it.” (web:Isa.46.11) with no fresh addressee onset at either point. The row closes on a second imperative address, “Listen to me, you stubborn-hearted, who are far from righteousness!” (web:Isa.46.12) -- שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֖י (oshb:Isa.46.12) -- matching the opening's שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3) at the accent-stripped tier, though the two summonses carry DIFFERENT vocatives -- אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֑ב (oshb:Isa.46.12, byte tier) here against בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier) at the opening -- which is the ground on which a repeated summons with a changed addressee closes a bracket rather than opening a fresh unit; the setumah terminating Isa.46.11 (single-witness, tier-3) marks a division at Isa.46.11|Isa.46.12 as corroboration for that reading, not as a driver for it, before the closing promise “I bring my righteousness near. It is not far off, and my salvation will not wait. I will grant salvation to Zion, my glory to Israel.” (web:Isa.46.13), the row's own closing verse before a fresh address to a new addressee opens the following row at web:Isa.47.1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival cut would open a fresh row at the appeal opening Isa.46.8 rather than reading it as bracketed inside the wider disputation running from Isa.46.3 to Isa.46.12.
